answer: Behavioral trail correlation works by scoring each identity's transaction history for coordination signals. A plume of near-identical activity timing across many accounts raises a shared-operator score, while each identity's distinct whisper of social links is cross-checked against known clusters. Flagged clusters draw a copper-trace audit of funding paths, and confirmed sybils lose accumulated reputation and future fee rebates. An attacker pays the full history-building cost per fake identity, then forfeits it all once correlation detects the pattern.
